topic: Determinants of price elasticity of demand
question: What is price elasticity of demand? Explain the factors that determine the price elasticity of demand for a commodity.
sources: Price elasticity of demand (standard microeconomic theory)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Price elasticity of demand is the degree of responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of a commodity, measured as percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price.

points.label: Substitutes
points.description: The more and closer the substitutes available, the more elastic the demand.
points.basis: Determinants of elasticity: availability of substitutes

points.label: Nature of the commodity and share of income
points.description: Necessities tend to have inelastic demand and luxuries elastic demand; goods on which a small share of income is spent (such as salt or matches) have inelastic demand.
points.basis: Determinants of elasticity: nature of commodity and proportion of income spent

points.label: Number of uses and postponement
points.description: A commodity with many uses has more elastic demand; demand is inelastic where consumption cannot be postponed.
points.basis: Determinants of elasticity: number of uses and urgency

points.label: Time period and habits
points.description: Demand is more elastic in the long run, as consumers find substitutes over time; goods consumed out of habit or addiction have inelastic demand.
points.basis: Determinants of elasticity: time and habits
